A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-regression experiments, uncertainty analyses on MNIST and CIFAR-10/SVHN, and ensemble-extraction evaluations on MNIST and ImageNet-v2, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds an original random-forest experiment in Appendix A.4 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The mask-based ensemble extraction, mask-diversity objective, spatial ensemble extraction, and weighted mutual information procedure are unchanged. Random forests provide another experimental model family; they do not introduce a new extraction algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy-regression task and MNIST, Dirty-MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN, and ImageNet-v2 coverage. Appendix A.4 explicitly replicates the existing toy task using random forests, without introducing a distinct dataset or task.

E2.justification: The corresponding neural-network comparisons retain the same ordinary ensembles, original single-model entropy baselines, and extracted ensembles. The new random-forest study varies forest size independently rather than adding a comparator against the extraction method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a configuration sweep using ensembles of 10 random forests, with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, or 64 trees per forest and maximum tree depth 3. Existing neural-network training settings, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The new random-forest sensitivity analysis tests whether uncertainty collapse also occurs outside neural networks as constituent ensemble size increases. Existing analyses of MLP width, extraction size, temperature scaling, and uncertainty metrics remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 1 already reports medians and 68%/95% confidence intervals in v1; v2 retains these and uses analogous intervals for the added random-forest results. No revised repeated-run counts, seed reporting, significance tests, or interval-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds random-forest results showing decreasing epistemic uncertainty and narrowing prediction bands as trees per forest increase. All six existing tables retain identical numerical values, and the original plotted results are retained, including v1 Figure 6 as v2 Figure 7.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 derives a relationship between variance-based uncertainty and mutual information under Gaussian, constant-covariance assumptions. Appendix A.3 adds a detailed convergence argument distinguishing empirical ensemble uncertainty from population mutual information. Section 2 also replaces the assumed posterior distribution with a more general training-induced parameter distribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion more carefully restrict theoretical justification to explicit ensembles of ensembles and present implicit ensembling in wider networks as a possible mechanism. The central contributions of demonstrating collapse and recovering uncertainty through extraction remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that extraction does not establish implicit ensembling as the cause and acknowledges alternative explanations. It adds a speculative NTK connection, interprets random-forest evidence as supporting broader applicability, and explains when variance-based and information-based uncertainty measures diverge. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion and its boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 documents the new random-forest experiment's tree counts, maximum depth, and number of forests. Previously supplied architectures, optimizers, hyperparameters, extraction settings, and pretrained-model sources are retained in the renumbered implementation and evaluation appendices.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around NTK theory, debates over uncertainty measures, and approximate posterior sampling. It adds comparisons with feature collapse, neural collapse, and Wortsman et al.'s subnetworks, while qualifying its explanatory contribution relative to Fellaji and Pennerath.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central theoretical narrative are substantially revised. Section 3 is reorganized into three subsections, implicit ensembling receives a dedicated Section 4, and a new theoretical appendix precedes the former Appendices A–D, now B–E. Interpretive passages and the conclusion are also rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel random-forest Figure 6 and publication headers. Existing figures and tables retain their displays with pagination changes; the previous supplementary Figure 6 becomes Figure 7. There is no broad graphical or tabular redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scientific caution by distinguishing demonstrated collapse from an unproven mechanism, and adds useful mathematical exposition and a non-neural validation experiment. The main empirical evidence remains unchanged. The theoretical expansion also contains a local inconsistency: Appendix A.3's text before Equation (20) gives entropy of the mean as the limit of mean entropy, whereas Equation (21) uses mean entropy. The net gain is clearer scope and supporting context, tempered by this mathematical error.
